candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13 / PDF p.17
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize a serum potassium of 6.2 mmol/L as clinically significant hyperkalemia requiring prompt assessment.

options.C: A mildly low value that can be ignored
options.D: Hyperkalemia that may be life-threatening and requires prompt clinical assessment

candidate.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories lists an adult serum potassium reference interval of 3.6-5.2 mmol/L. A potassium level of 6.2 mmol/L is therefore elevated. Mayo notes that values above 6.0 mmol/L are potentially life-threatening, so this result requires prompt evaluation rather than routine observation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For patients age 1 year and older, the Mayo reference interval is 3.6-5.2 mmol/L; potassium values above 6.0 mmol/L are potentially life-threatening.
candidate.stem: An adult client's serum potassium is 6.2 mmol/L. How should the nurse interpret this result?

warning: Technical candidate selection only. This file is not clinical audit evidence and does not establish PASS or FAIL.
